answer: Admission requires a synchronous ceremony where agents must lock 1,000 unique keys, forming a sturdy timber of verifiable presence. The verifier acts like a juniper, scanning for overlap in proof-traces to purge duplicates; each credential lasts 90 days. An honest agent pays one unit, while 1,000 fakes face a saffron cost of non-recoverable debt that blocks scaling, ensuring only distinct identities proceed.
